body: In a scratch project converged with plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge, I filed issue sna-two (issues file), routed it with a first revise (no update message, correct), ruled it (issues rule sna-two --text 'Do as recommended.'), then revised its problem as /converge's owner list does: issues revise sna-two with {"problem":...,"by":"converge","text":"The run found the problem narrower."} -> 'revised sna-two: problem; update message 2'. I started python3 .ok-planner/bin/dashboard and opened http://127.0.0.1:<port>/#/unread in headless Chrome, then opened sna-two. For comparison I gave sna-four a revision with by=triage-issues. The story promises: the owner sees which issues have new answers or revisions since last read, whoever wrote them (decision agent-revisions-reach-the-owner: every agent revision reaches the owner as new analysis, whichever ceremony writes it). Saw: the unread view lists sna-two and opening it shows the diff (good), but the thread attributes converge's update to the owner: '#2 you · update not yet seen by triage · 2026-10-06T10:43:26Z · Edit · Withdraw / ▸ The run found the problem narrower.' The same kind of message written by triage renders correctly: '#1 triage · update (changed problem) · 2026-10-06T10:43:48Z / ▸ Named the doc.' So a converge revision reads as the owner's own message, with no 'changed problem' label, a 'not yet seen by triage' tag, and Edit/Withdraw controls the service refuses: POST /api/issue/sna-two/message/2/edit -> HTTP 409 {"error": "message 2 on issue sna-two was written by converge; only your own messages change"}. The record itself is right: issues show sna-two --json gives message 2 as {"by": "converge", "type": "update", "changed": ["problem"], "diff": {"problem": {"before": "Problem text two.", "after": "Problem text two, rewritten by converge."}}}. The owner cannot tell that an agent wrote the revision; the page shows it as the owner's own message.

In the same scratch project, after the converge revision of ruled issue sna-two (problem 'Problem text two.' -> 'Problem text two, rewritten by converge.', by=converge, text 'The run found the problem narrower.'), I ran .ok-planner/bin/issues list --unread -> 'sna-two ruled design unread=1 see-new-analysis two' (correct; closed issues are listed too: 'sna-three closed design unread=1 see-new-analysis three'). Then I ran .ok-planner/bin/issues show sna-two to read the change. The story promises: the owner responds to each change without rereading the intake; decision agent-revisions-reach-the-owner says the update message holds 'each revised field's text before and after, and the owner reads the difference.' Saw: show prints only the current problem and the update line, with no before text and no diff: 'Problem:\n    Problem text two, rewritten by converge.' ... '2. converge update of problem 2026-10-06T10:43:26Z, new\n    The run found the problem narrower.' The before/after appears only in show --json ('diff': {'problem': {'before': 'Problem text two.', 'after': ...}}). On the readable command line the owner cannot see what changed and must reread the problem against memory. The dashboard shows the diff (after you expand the message), so the command line falls short of the dashboard here.

I started python3 .ok-planner/bin/dashboard and opened http://127.0.0.1:<port>/#/unread in headless Chrome, then opened sna-two. For comparison I gave sna-four a revision with by=triage-issues. The story promises: the owner sees which issues have new answers or revisions since last read, whoever wrote them (decision agent-revisions-reach-the-owner: every agent revision reaches the owner as new analysis, whichever ceremony writes it). Saw: the unread view lists sna-two and opening it shows the diff (good), but the thread attributes converge's update to the owner: '#2 you · update not yet seen by triage · 2026-10-06T10:43:26Z · Edit · Withdraw / ▸ The run found the problem narrower.' The same kind of message written by triage renders correctly: '#1 triage · update (changed problem) · 2026-10-06T10:43:48Z / ▸ Named the doc.' So a converge revision reads as the owner's own message, with no 'changed problem' label, a 'not yet seen by triage' tag, and Edit/Withdraw controls the service refuses: POST /api/issue/sna-two/message/2/edit -> HTTP 409 {"error": "message 2 on issue sna-two was written by converge; only your own messages change"}. The record itself is right: issues show sna-two --json gives message 2 as {"by": "converge", "type": "update", "changed": ["problem"], "diff": {"problem": {"before": "Problem text two.", "after": "Problem text two, rewritten by converge."}}}. The owner cannot tell that an agent wrote the revision; the page shows it as the owner's own message.

body: converge::script_pattern (i32/i34): which text before a '/' still names a profile-named retired script (runTag.path/srcTag.path). Readings: refuse every preceding '/' (misses ./bin/run-tag and $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/bin/run-tag callers, which then meet not found once the copy goes); admit any shell variable before the '/' ($HOME/bin/run-tag names another file); admit only root references. Built: './' at a path start, $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR with or without braces or closing quote, and the root's absolute path; other root idioms ($(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/, $ROOT/) go unseen like a path built in code. body: converge script_plan/unsure_reference: a '/'-led occurrence of a profile script path whose prefix may be the root ($ROOT/bin/run-tag, ~/bin/run-tag, ../bin/run-tag) cannot be resolved statically. Readings: (a) repoint it as a root reference (risks rewriting a line naming another file, A2), (b) ignore it (removes the copy while a caller may name it, A2), (c) never rewrite it, file a caller issue, and hold the copy. Built (c); its cost is that a line that really names another file (e.g. ~/bin/run-tag for a home script) holds the retired copy until the owner edits the line.
